Name: view_disagreement_escalation_trajectory_judges
Title: Counterfactual-View Disagreement Escalation for Robust Web-Agent Trajectory Judges
Short Hypothesis: Using View1 (with CoT) vs View2 (no CoT) disagreement as a trigger for selective escalation to a stricter, evidence-anchored rubric prompt will improve the precision-recall-cost frontier for web-agent trajectory judges -- because disagreement concentrates cases where the judge relies on narrative fields not supported by observable evidence.
Related Work: AgentRewardBench (Lu et al., 2025) benchmarks trajectory judges on 1,302 expert-annotated web-agent trajectories. Gaming the Judge (Khalifa et al., 2025) shows CoT rewriting inflates false positives. WebJudge/An Illusion of Progress (Xue et al., 2025) proposes rubric-based evidence-anchored evaluation. DAFE/CLEV (Badshah et al., 2025) uses dynamic arbitration triggered by judge disagreement. No prior work uses counterfactual input-view disagreement (with-CoT vs no-CoT) as a selective escalation trigger for trajectory judges.

benchmarks: AgentRewardBench (1,302 trajectories, 811 failure cases in test set)
notes: Fully prompt-based -- works entirely via Gemini API
Core innovation is a prompting strategy, model-agnostic
Existing results: delta-FPR reduced from +11.71% to +4.31% (63% improvement)
Long trajectories may need long-context Gemini calls
